description:
kit flow shows where the work stands, from the issues to releases

Usage:
  kit flow [--fresh] [--text | --json | --jq] [--all | [--mine] [--others] [--owner=<login>…]]
  kit flow --stages
  kit flow --me
  kit flow --capabilities
  kit flow --quota
  kit flow --marks
  kit flow issues [--json | --jq] [--cached] [--fresh] [--today] [--all | [--mine] [--others] [--owner=<login>…]]
  kit flow incoming [--json | --jq] [--cached]
  kit flow changes [--json | --jq] [--cached] [--fresh] [--all | [--mine] [--others] [--owner=<login>…]] [<number>…]
  kit flow builds [--json | --jq] [--cached]
  kit flow releases [--json | --jq] [--cached]

Its whole page is the resource kit://help/flow.

all.description: every issue and pull request (the default); it stands alone

cached.description: with --json and a stage, prints what that stage printed last here with the same arguments, whatever its age, and reads nothing; refuses when it has printed nothing yet

capabilities.description: prints what the primary's forge can do, as one JSON object: {contract, forge, provider, features}, each feature native or none, as modules/bash/forge.sh declares them; it asks nothing

fresh.description: reads the open issues and pull requests afresh, not the snapshot of the last minute

jq.description: the same JSON, formatted by jq for a person

json.description: the picture as one JSON object, each stage under its name

marks.description: prints a mark per stage, as one JSON object, which changes when what the stage draws does: read again, a mark that differs says the stage is stale; on GitHub, nothing changed costs no request

me.description: prints the caller's login on the primary's forge, the login --mine and --others match

mine.description: only the caller's: assigned issues, and opened pull requests

number.description: only these pull requests, by number or issue closed: #7

owner.description: only the named login's; give it once or more, or join the logins with :, --owner=a:b

quota.description: prints the caller's rate limits on the primary's forge, as one JSON array: each forge's {forge, limits}, each limit {name, limit, remaining, reset}; reading them costs a request at most. A forge without rate limits gives none, and asks nothing

stage.description: issues: every open issue, oldest first: in the backlog, or underway, closed by an open pull request or named by a branch: who works on each, and where; incoming: what fetching every remote brought: default-branch commits, branches new and gone; changes: the open pull requests, each with the issues it closes; builds: the runs not owned by any pull request: the default branch, tags, schedules; releases: the releases on the forge, newest first

stages.description: prints the stages the picture draws, one per line, in order

text.description: prints the picture as text, even on a terminal

today.description: only the issues opened in the last 24 hours

name: flow
title: kit flow

description:
kit packages lists the packages in reach, and changes which are active

Usage:
  kit packages [--active | --inactive] [--text | --json | --jq] [<package>…]
  kit packages --stages
  kit packages --marks
  kit packages packages [--text | --json | --jq]

Its whole page is the resource kit://help/packages.

inactive.description: the packages that are not active, excluded ones among them

jq.description: the same JSON, formatted by jq for a person

json.description: one JSON object per package: name, origin, state, and description; with packages, the stage's document, {rows, errors}

marks.description: prints the stage's mark, as one JSON object, which changes when kit.yml or .kit/packages/ does

package.description: a name, such as style/bash, or a glob, such as 'style/*'

stages.description: prints the stages, one per line: packages

subcommand.description: packages: the stage: a row per package in reach, {name, state, origin, depends, includes, dependents, bundles, description}, keyed by its name; dependents are the active packages that depend on it, and bundles the active ones that include it

text.description: lists the packages as text, even on a terminal; with packages, the stage as a table

name: packages
title: kit packages

description:
kit syntax prints a verb's grammar as JSON, and checks its header

Usage:
  kit syntax [--check | --list] [<verb>…]
  kit syntax <verb> --choices=<argument> [<answer>…]
  kit syntax <verb> --extend [<answer>…]
  kit syntax <verb> --match [<word>…]

Its whole page is the resource kit://help/syntax.

answer.description: an argument answered already, or a subcommand word chosen

check.description: prints no JSON; names each fault in the header, and fails

choices.description: prints that argument's choices instead, one per line

extend.description: prints the arguments the verb learns from the answers

list.description: prints no JSON; one line per verb: verb, purpose, group, tab-separated

match.description: judges the words as the guard judges a command line

verb.description: the verbs to print; none prints every verb

word.description: the words of the command line to judge, after kit <verb>

description:
kit work starts or resumes work on issues

Usage:
  kit work <reference>…

Its whole page is the resource kit://help/work.

pr.description: adds the issues to one of the caller's own open pull requests instead: each is assigned to the caller and closed by it
